content:
julie: FYI — customer ACME reports they got charged for a bunch of 5xx tokens when their iOS app went to background during streaming. They claim the client never received an error, app just suspended.

omar: do we have a ticket link? any sample trace/span ids?

julie: ticket #54321, span id: span_0a1b2c3d. They attached a short network capture and our gateway logs. gist excerpt below.

cheng: past issues like this were often client-side half-close -> kernel RST -> proxy surfaces EPIPE which our billing heuristics treat as server 5xx. Could be same.

julie: here's the gateway log snippet they sent:

```
2026-03-10T14:12:08.123Z gateway-01 INFO req=span_0a1b2c3d upstream_send: wrote 2 chunks
2026-03-10T14:12:10.451Z gateway-01 WARN req=span_0a1b2c3d write_error: writev: EPIPE
2026-03-10T14:12:10.452Z gateway-01 ERROR req=span_0a1b2c3d classify: upstream_error_code=EPIPE mapped_status=502 billing_tag=5xx
```

anna: so billing tags it as 5xx? customer is requesting credit. We need to confirm root cause before approving.

mike: can we reproduce locally by simulating iOS suspend? Maybe TCP RST from client side when sleep.

omar: simplest repro: open streaming endpoint from curl and close socket mid-stream. But need to mimic iOS behavior where TCP stack sends RST upon app suspend in some network conditions. I can try netem + tcpkill.

cheng: also try reproducer with chunked encoding and --no-buffer to force streaming. sample: 

```
# start streaming request (server will stream tokens slowly)
curl -v -N -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/respond -d '{"prompt":"long stream test","stream":true}' &
# after a few chunks, kill client to simulate abrupt close
sleep 3; pkill -f "curl -v -N" # or use tcpkill to send RSTs
```

julie: customer included tcpdump: they show client IP sending RST shortly after last ACK. excerpt below.

```
10:12:10.450000 IP 10.1.2.3.54321 > 34.56.78.90.443: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
10:12:10.450012 IP 34.56.78.90.443 > 10.1.2.3.54321: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
```

mike: that aligns with EPIPE on write. The open question: should that be billed as 5xx? Historically billing heuristics try to detect client-initiated aborts and mark as non-billable/neutral, but some edge cases misclassify when proxy can't reliably differentiate RST vs upstream failure.

anna: what metric or log do we need to justify a credit?

cheng: we look for upstream errors (model/container crash), gateway internal error, or customer-side RST. If only EPIPE and no upstream error codes (500s, OOM logs, liveness failures), it's client abort. But our current rule flags EPIPE as upstream error if it happens before any non-EOF trailer. Need clearer boundary: if last_sent_chunk_timestamp < 5s and client sent RST immediately, classify as client-abort.

omar: proposed quick repro plan for SRE:
- spin a small local dev deployment of the streaming runtime (dev-runtime:latest)
- run a streaming request with small token cadence (server waits 1s between chunks)
- use tc/netem to emulate mobile NAT timeouts (delay, conn-close)
- send RST from client and capture gateway log + stderr of runtime

mike: can we get a deterministic curl-based repro that we can drop in the ticket steps? we need something support can run on macOS so CS can verify with customer.

cheng: macOS repro using hping3 to send RST is nice because you don't need root for tcpkill? actually hping3 needs root. Another approach: use socat to send and then close raw FD. Example:

```
# 1) start stream
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/respond -d '{"prompt":"..., stream:true"}' &
# 2) find curl PID and fd, then kill -9 PID to force RST
sleep 3; kill -9 $CURL_PID
```

julie: customer says their app doesn't crash — it just goes to background and OS decides to teardown the TCP connection (RST) quickly. They argue that's a client abort and shouldn't be billed.

anna: policy perspective: we don't bill for requests where client aborted before model produced content beyond the prefix? We need exact threshold. Ops historically credits when client abort occurs before more than 1 token produced. But that's vague.

mike: for this specific incident: logs show two chunks were written, timestamp 14:12:08, and EPIPE at 14:12:10. We need to count tokens/chunks and measure whether meaningful output was delivered. If customer consumed the first chunk(s), they shouldn't be charged for model compute after they've aborted. If they didn't get last chunk, only partial tokens billed should match delivered tokens. Billing system currently charges for tokens attempted to be written by runtime, not only delivered tokens — which causes disputes.

cheng: fix proposals:
- short term: classify EPIPE where tcpdump shows client RST within 1s of write_error as client-abort -> mark billing_tag=client_aborted (non-5xx)
- medium term: change billing to bill only for confirmed delivered bytes/token acks from gateway layer (incremental acking)
- longer term: add a small client-side header X-Client-Session-Id we can correlate, plus SDK update to send a final FIN-friendly close or explicit cancel so we can distinguish app background vs network RST.

omar: I can craft a patch for the quick heuristic by EOD and run unit + integration test. Will post PR.

julie: customer asked for repro steps they can run. Can we share the macOS curl + kill-9 sequence? Might be enough. Also offer a temporary credit pending root cause.

anna: approve small credit while SRE verifies reproducibility. Please document exact token counts and attach logs.

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0543 by julie; assigned to omar and cheng. SLA: 72h.

julie: thanks — I'll reply to the customer with reproducer and offer credit. Will attach our plan and ETA for fix. :thumbsup:

omar: I'll post the PR link once ready and add integration test that simulates client RST and checks billing tag.

mike: also add a metric/emitter that counts EPIPEs and how many are tagged 5xx vs client_aborted so we can measure regressions.

julie: leaving this thread open until PR and credit are done.
